_notes.paper_claim: The paper reports that unlimited sensing gives at least 30 dB lower recovery MSE than a conventional ADC with the same bit budget, across DR = 10, 20, 30 lambda and 3-15 bits (Fig. 2; also Section IV: 'consistent >= 30 dB gains'). The 30.0 under results.us_sres is that lower bound, not a point estimate.

paper_fig2_gains_read_from_plot_db.note: Approximate gaps between the conventional-ADC and USF MSE curves of Fig. 2. Fig. 2's conventional ADC spans the full signal range (no clipping) and the waveforms carry no additive sensor noise, so these are not on this gym's scale.

_notes.setup_differences: This gym compares against the equal-range clipping ADC of Section V-A1 (Fig. 5) instead of Fig. 2's full-range ADC, adds Gaussian thermal noise (std 0.03 lambda) before both ADCs (Section III, challenge C1), uses a known Gaussian pulse (sigma = 20 samples) instead of the calibrated ToF kernel, randomises spike positions, separation (60-90 samples), weak/strong ratio (7-13) and order, and scores 200 hidden scenes per setting (paper: 5000 trials of real-kernel waveforms).
_notes.paper_tables: Tables I-II report PSNR of about 39-41 dB for 3-bit hardware-derived recoveries; hardware waveforms are not available, so these are not targets here.

synthetic_lowbit_hdr_dr10.description: Recover the HDR waveform and both off-grid spike times of a K=2 weak/strong pulse pair (N=501) from 3-bit modulo samples at ||g||_inf = 10 lambda. Fig. 2 signal model at 10x dynamic range with 3-bit sensing.

mse_gain_over_conventional_db.description: Primary metric (Fig. 2 quantity): 10 log10 of the waveform MSE of the conventional clipping-ADC recovery, computed by the evaluator, over the method's waveform MSE, pooled over the slice's scenes.

psnr_db.description: Mean per-scene waveform PSNR (peak = ||g||_inf), the reconstruction-quality figure of Tables I and II; complements the pooled gain with typical-scene quality.

time_mae_samples.description: Mean absolute error of both recovered spike times (time-delay estimation, Tables I-II), in samples.

weak_tau_mae_samples.description: Spike-time error of the weak reflection only: the weak target is what coarse quantization buries (Figs. 1 and 9).

separation_error_samples.description: Error of the recovered inter-spike separation (the inter-object separation error reported in Section V-B and VI), in samples.
